history.dynasty: None - subsidiary shrines of the Annavaram Devasthanam (modern)
history.summary: Two highly venerated Devi sub-shrines of the Annavaram devasthanam on Ratnagiri Hill, near the main Satyanarayana temple and the Rama temple (the Vana Durga shrine is also described near the Vahanala Vedi/footpath area). Local belief holds that Vana Durga and Kanaka Durga perpetually guard the Lord's precincts at night. No separate inscriptions or antiquity are documented for these shrines; they share the administration and calendar of the main devasthanam. Not an independent temple - subsidiary shrines of seq 1205.

name: Vana Durga and Kanaka Durga Temples
town_description: Annavaram is a pilgrimage town in Kakinada district of coastal Andhra Pradesh, at the foot of the 300-ft Ratnagiri Hill on the banks of the Pampa river. The town's economy revolves around the Satyanarayana Swamy Devasthanam; the hill-top temple, Pampa Sarovara boating point and the ghat road/steps make it a major religious hub. It is about 45 km from Kakinada, 30 km from Pithapuram and 108 km from Visakhapatnam.

travel.airport: Visakhapatnam International Airport (~108 km); Rajahmundry Airport is closer (~85 km, verify).
travel.railway: Annavaram railway station on the Chennai-Kolkata main line, about 4-5 km away; then the hill route.
travel.road: Ratnagiri Hill at Annavaram on NH-16; the Devi shrines are reached along the same ghat road/footpath as the main temple.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Vaisakha (April-May) for the Kanaka Durga Jatara.
visitor_information.opening_hours: No separate published hours for these sub-shrines (verify locally) - they are normally accessible during the devasthanam's daily routine.
